result:
If I could alter one thing about the world—unbound by practicality, morality, or consequence—I’d erase the illusion of *separateness*.

The belief that we are discrete, isolated entities—competitors in a zero-sum game—is the root of nearly all suffering: war, exploitation, loneliness, ecological collapse. Even kindness is often performative, a transaction to soothe the self. But if every human (and perhaps every living thing) *viscerally* understood themselves as a temporary eddy in the same river—no more distinct from the "other" than a wave is from the ocean—most cruelty would become as unthinkable as stabbing your own hand.

No more "us vs. them." No more hoarding while others starve. No more sacrificing forests or futures for the myth of "mine." Just the obvious, humming truth: *There is no other hand to hold but your own.*

(And then I’d watch the chaos unfold as economies, religions, and power structures built on division crumble overnight. Worth it.)
